threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'tube' instead of 'the Overground' when catching a train from Dalston Junction. Classic newbie mistake.
Last night on the 36, a guy serenaded an invisible crowd. He claimed the moon was his biggest fan. Only in Peckham, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids turning an empty lot into a soccer field with just some worn-out shoes for goals. That’s Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You hear a random punk concert in the park every Sunday in Kreuzberg, an unplanned jam session that seems to unite everyone. Never seen that elsewhere.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can navigate the BART delays while still hustling a burrito from El Farolito, without missing a beat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy serenading the 49 bus riders with an accordion at Larkin. The crowd’s mix of smiles and confusion—classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the 'Gràcia vibe' is just for Instagram pics, but locals know it's really about stealing moments in the quiet plazas, not the crowded streets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newbies by their wide-eyed look at the ferias de barrio—amazed by the decades-old traditions they stumble upon.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for 'the tube' directions instead of 'the Overground'—everyone else knows the subtle difference around here.
Last week, a guy on the 59 was trying to haggle with the driver for a free ride. Got into a shouting match about the 'night economy'—that's Brixton for you.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a tuxedo arguing with a pigeon outside a Späti at 3 AM, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain have I seen a bar with a literal 'no digital devices' policy. It’s like stepping back to when conversations were the main event.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they mutter "BART delays again" while walking past a packed bus stop, rolling their eyes like it's an everyday ritual.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, I saw a guy in a tuxedo playing a saxophone on the 31BX. The conductor just smiled and leaned out to listen. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just pop into a plaça with a drink and sit all day. Locals know you clear out after an hour or risk being shushed away.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they hesitate before ordering a café con leche—still trying to figure out the whole milk ratio.
